title: Assam
sub: From Assampedia, the free Assam encyclopedia
body:
Assam is a state in north-eastern India, south of the eastern Himalayas, along the Brahmaputra and Barak river valleys. It is known for Assam tea, its silk, the one-horned rhinoceros, and the Bihu festivals.

Geography

Assam is divided by the Brahmaputra river, which flows from east to west through the state. The Barak Valley lies in the south, and the Karbi Anglong and Dima Hasao hills rise in the centre. Kaziranga National Park, on the Brahmaputra's banks, is famous for the Indian one-horned rhinoceros.

History

The region was ruled in ancient times by kingdoms including Kamarupa, and later by the Ahom kingdom, which ruled for about 600 years from the 13th century. Assam became part of British India in 1826, after the Treaty of Yandabo, and a state of independent India in 1947.

Culture

The main festivals are the three Bihus — Rongali (Bohag) Bihu in spring, Kongali (Kati) Bihu in autumn, and Bhogali (Magh) Bihu in winter. Assamese, Bodo and Bengali are widely spoken, and the state's classical dance form is Sattriya.
extra:
Districts and administration

Assam is divided into districts grouped under divisions, with Dispur as the seat of government. Guwahati is the state's largest city and commercial centre, while Upper Assam (Jorhat, Dibrugarh, Sivasagar) is the heart of the tea industry and Ahom heritage.

Economy

Tea, oil and natural gas, agriculture (especially rice), silk, bamboo and tourism are major parts of the economy. Digboi, in Upper Assam, is home to one of Asia's oldest oil refineries, and the state is India's largest tea-growing region.

Wildlife and nature

Assam's national parks — Kaziranga, Manas, Nameri, Orang and Dibru-Saikhowa — protect the one-horned rhinoceros, tigers, elephants, golden langurs and hundreds of bird species, in the Brahmaputra floodplains and foothills.
